extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and researchers interested in censorship, media law, and human rights in Iraq
extracted.subtask_description: A country-level encyclopedia summary of legal provisions, constitutional guarantees, historical practices, and Internet censorship related to freedom of expression and media in Iraq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 215
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who produces, imports, exports or obtains a picture, written material or sign with intent to trade, distribute, display or exhibit such material, which, by its nature, endangers the public security or brings the country into disrepute unless he was acting in good faith is punishable by detention plus a fine not exceeding 300 dinars or by one of those penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the penal code provisions addressing limits on materials that 'endanger the public security' or 'bring the country into disrepute'; penalty options include detention and fines (<= 300 dinars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 220
rubrics_metrics.description: If five or more people are assembled in a public place, thereby endangering the public security and the public authorities order them to disperse, any person who is given that order and refuses to comply with it is punishable by a period of detention not exceeding 1 year plus a fine not exceeding 100 dinars or by one of those penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminalizes refusal to disperse when an assembly of five or more is deemed to endanger public security; establishes detention (<=1 year) and fine (<=100 dinars) as penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 403
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who produces, imports, publishes, possesses, obtains or translates a book, printed or other written material, drawing, picture, film, symbol or other thing that violates the public integrity or decency with intent to exploit or distribute such material is punishable by a period of detention not exceeding 2 years plus a fine not exceeding 200 dinars or by one of those penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies equally to advertising, public display, sale, hire, distribution or submission for distribution; if the offense is committed with intent to deprave, that is an aggravating circumstance. Penalty: detention (<=2 years) and fine (<=200 dinars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 404
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who himself or through some mechanical means sings or broadcasts in a public place obscene or indecent songs or statements is punishable by a period of detention not exceeding 1 year or by a fine not exceeding 100 dinars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalizes public singing or broadcasting of 'obscene or indecent' content; provides detention or fine options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 434 (Insult)
rubrics_metrics.description: Insult is the imputation to another of something dishonourable or disrespectful or the hurting of his feelings even though it does not include an imputation to him of a particular matter. Any person who insults another is punishable by a period of detention not exceeding 1 year plus a fine not exceeding 100 dinars or by one of those penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing an insult in a newspaper/publication/medium is considered an aggravating circumstance, increasing seriousness under the penal code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 438 (Privacy disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following persons are punishable by a period of detention not exceeding 1 year plus a fine not exceeding 100 dinars or by one of those penalties: (1) Any person who publishes in any way a picture, remark or information in respect of the private or family life of another, even though such information is true and such publication causes him offense. (2) Any person other than those mentioned in Paragraph 328 who is privy to information contained in a letter, telex or telephone conversation and he discloses such information to a person other than for whom it is intended and such disclosure causes harm to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects private/family life and private communications from publication or unauthorized disclosure even if the information is true; establishes detention (<=1 year) and fine (<=100 dinars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitution Article 7
rubrics_metrics.description: No entity or program, under any name, may adopt racism, terrorism, the calling of others infidels, ethnic cleansing, or incite, facilitate, glorify, promote, or justify thereto, especially the Saddamist Baath in Iraq and its symbols, regardless of the name that it adopts. This may not be part of the political pluralism in Iraq. This will be organized by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional prohibition on adopting or promoting racism/terrorism/ethnic cleansing and on glorifying the former Ba'ath; these are excluded from permissible political pluralism and are to be regulated by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitution Articles 36 and 38 (freedom of expression/press/assembly)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state guarantees in a way that does not violate public order and morality: a. Freedom of expression, through all means. b. Freedom of press, printing, advertisement, media and publication. c. Freedom of assembly and peaceful demonstration. This shall be regulated by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional guarantees of speech, press, and assembly are explicitly qualified by the restriction 'in a way that does not violate public order and morality' and are subject to regulation by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitution Article 40 (communications privacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The freedom of communication, and mail, telegraphic, electronic, and telephonic correspondence, and other correspondence shall be guaranteed and may not be monitored, wiretapped or disclosed except for legal and security necessity and by a judicial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects communications from monitoring or disclosure except where legally necessary for security and authorized by a judicial decision, establishing a judicial-authorization requirement for surveillance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet censorship: ONI findings and constitutional limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The ONI found no evidence of filtering from Iraq in August 2009 in all 4 areas for which the government tests political filtering, social filtering, conflict/security, and monitoring of Internet tools. Iraq's constitution provides for the rights of freedom of speech and press, and the government respects these rights in practice. Those freedoms are provided so long that it doesn't violate public order and morality or express support for the banned Baath Party or for altering the country's borders by violent means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes low Internet penetration (17.6% at end of 2013) and frames online freedoms as subject to the same constitutional qualifications (public order/morality, bans on Ba'ath support, or advocacy of violent border changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2003 reversion to 1988 penal code (with revisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2003, the Iraqi penal code was reverted to its 1988 edition with some revisions drafted by Paul Bremer and later the Iraqi national government. Several provisions in the current penal code address the limitations placed on the freedom of the press and communicative media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual note explaining the legal basis for the cited penal provisions and their role in regulating press/media freedoms after the 2003 changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saddam-era censorship and Revolutionary Command Council powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Saddam Hussein (1979–2003) political criticism which undermined the Ba'ath party was illegal. The Revolutionary Command Council (per the 1990 constitution) had the right to prohibit anything they felt harmed 'national unity', the 'objectives of the People' or their 'achievements'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical standard showing prior expansive grounds for prohibition of expression (national unity/objectives/achievements) used to justify censorship during the Ba'athist regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kingdom of Iraq Constitution Articles 12, 13, 15 (early guarantees and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 12: 'Freedom of expression of opinion, liberty of publication, of meeting together, and of forming and joining associations' ... in accordance with whatever laws were enacted by the national government. Article 13: guarantees freedom to practise religion and freedom of conscience provided such forms of worship do not conflict with the maintenance of order and discipline or public morality. Article 15: 'All postal and telegraphic correspondence and all telephonic communications shall be secret and free from censorship or detention, except in such circumstances and in such manner as may be prescribed by law.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical constitutional provisions that guaranteed expression and correspondence while allowing exceptions 'in accordance with laws' or 'as prescribed by law', demonstrating a pattern of rights qualified by public order and statutory exceptions.
